title: How AI is transforming prototyping and interface design
description: From sketch to working prototype: how AI changed prototyping, which tools emerged and why the designer's role becomes more strategic.
updateNote: Revised in October 2026: I added what has changed since publication and a new visual to explain the central idea.

related.title: Clint Scale
related.body: In practice: an explorable design system, with tokens, components, contrast and governance.

blocks.text: A few years ago, imagining that a hand-drawn sketch could automatically turn into a working prototype sounded like science fiction. Today, that reality is just a few clicks away. Artificial intelligence (AI) has not only sped up the design process, it has also redefined how we create digital experiences.
But then the big question comes up: will AI replace designers?

The short answer: no. The full answer: AI didn't come to replace us, but to amplify our potential, removing repetitive tasks and letting us focus on what really matters, creating intuitive and engaging experiences for users.
AI tools that are revolutionizing design
In recent years, several tools started integrating AI to optimize prototyping and interface design. Here are some of the most promising:

blocks.caption: AI shortens the path between an idea and something you can test.

items: Lovable, an AI-powered interface generator that suggests elements automatically, adjusts layouts and lets you test different UX/UI approaches in record time.

Figma with AI Plugins, Figma, one of the most popular tools among designers, now has plugins that use AI to suggest layouts, optimize spacing and even generate more natural, contextual placeholder text.
Uizard, turns hand-drawn scribbles into working prototypes, speeding up the early design phase and making brainstorming easier.
Galileo AI, generates interfaces automatically from text descriptions, turning abstract ideas into interactive prototypes effortlessly.

blocks.text: AI and its impact on the creative process

Automating mechanical tasks, like aligning components, setting spacing and adjusting colors, lets designers spend more time on strategy, accessibility and user experience. AI also democratizes design, letting professionals without advanced technical knowledge validate ideas quickly.

blocks.caption: The time AI frees up goes back to what matters in design.

blocks.text: But at the same time, AI also challenges us to redefine our role. If we used to spend hours adjusting pixels, now we need to go deeper into user experience, inclusive design and curating meaningful interfaces.
Prototyping in 2026: from click to code
When I wrote this piece, AI helped with parts of the process. Today tools like Figma Make, v0, Lovable and Claude generate working prototypes, with data and navigation, from good context.
That changes when the user comes in. You can test a working idea much earlier.

blocks.caption: A working prototype shortens the path to the user. But testing is still the step that validates.

blocks.text: The catch is not confusing polish with validation. A prototype that looks finished easily convinces the team, and that's why it needs to go through user testing before it becomes a decision.
The future of design: more strategic and human

What sets a great designer apart isn't the tool they use, but how they use it. AI doesn't eliminate the need for designers, it invites us to take on a more strategic role. The future of design won't just be about creating pretty interfaces, but about using technology intelligently to boost creativity and empathy.
And you, are you already using AI in your design process? How has it been going? Share in the comments!
